title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, AI Hypercomputer, and Prebuilt AI
bodyMarkdown:
## Provisioning AI is mostly a build-versus-buy decision

The ML objectives in the provisioning domain ask you to do two things: stand up the managed platform for end-to-end ML workflows, and know when no custom model is needed at all. The decision ladder is: prebuilt API first, a foundation model or AutoML second, custom training on accelerators last. At each rung, the exam checks that you pick the managed component rather than hand-rolling it on VMs.

## Product naming

The platform formerly called Vertex AI is now the **Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform**; the [platform documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/start/introduction-unified-platform) uses that name throughout (URL paths still say `vertex-ai`, and older exam material still says "Vertex AI"). Treat both names as the same product. Its capabilities include **Agent Studio**, **Model Garden**, **Notebooks**, **Feature Store**, **Model Registry**, **Training** (custom and AutoML), **Prediction** (online and batch), **Pipelines**, **Experiments**, **Model Monitoring** and **Evaluation**, with Gemini, open, and partner models.

## Pipelines for repeatable ML workflows

[Pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/pipelines/introduction) orchestrate ML workflows as managed, serverless DAGs. They are the answer whenever a scenario describes preprocessing, training, evaluation and conditional deployment that must be reproducible.

- **SDKs:** Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) and TensorFlow Extended (TFX) are supported, with custom components or the prebuilt Google Cloud Pipeline Components.
- **Lineage:** ML Metadata tracks pipeline artifacts, so you can trace a deployed model to its data, parameters and code.
- **Execution control:** execution caching skips unchanged steps, failure policies and retries are configurable, and conditions implement "deploy only if the evaluation metric passes".
- **Triggers:** the scheduler API runs pipelines on a schedule, and Pub/Sub can trigger them on events.

A VM with a bash script has no lineage, caching or retry, chained Cloud Functions are a brittle hand-built orchestrator, and BigQuery scheduled queries run SQL, not multi-stage training. Related components: **Model Registry** versions and governs trained models, **Feature Store** serves consistent features for training and inference, **Experiments** compares runs, **Model Monitoring** catches drift after deployment.

## Preparing data and gluing workloads together

- **Training data.** Custom training reads from Cloud Storage, BigQuery or managed datasets ([training overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/training-overview)). The [data preparation overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/training/data-preparation-overview) says you can use BigQuery data directly without moving it. With a [managed dataset](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/training/using-managed-datasets), the training container receives `AIP_DATA_FORMAT` (`jsonl`, `csv` or `bigquery`) and `AIP_TRAINING_DATA_URI`, which is a `bq://project.dataset.table` URI for BigQuery data, so no CSV export is needed; do not build a nightly export-to-bucket copy when BigQuery is the system of record.
- **[Feature Store](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/featurestore/latest/overview)** keeps feature source data in **BigQuery tables and views**, organized as feature groups (mapping to the source) and feature views (materializing features to an online store for low-latency serving). Offline serving for training reads BigQuery directly with no extra copy and supports point-in-time lookups of historical values (preventing leakage and training-serving skew). There is no separate offline store to copy into.
- **Skew: prevent versus detect.** Google notes that [training-serving skew](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/new-vertex-ai-feature-store-bigquery-powered-genai-ready) often occurs when data is handled differently in training and serving pipelines; shared, governed feature definitions address that cause. [Model Monitoring](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/model-monitoring/overview) only detects it: it alerts when the production feature distribution deviates from training beyond your threshold. "Same features for training and inference" means Feature Store; "alert me on skew" means Model Monitoring.
- **[Cloud Run functions](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/functions/comparison)** are Cloud Run services deployed from source, triggered by HTTP or events (Eventarc, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Firestore). HTTP functions run up to 60 minutes, event-driven ones up to 9. In ML they are glue (start a pipeline when a file lands), not an orchestrator or a training environment.

## Explaining and auditing model decisions

Altostrat's requirement for "auditable AI with explainable decisions" needs four tools, one per audit question.

| Question | Tool |
|---|---|
| Why did the model score this input this way? | [Feature attributions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/overview) (Vertex Explainable AI): each feature's contribution to one prediction, online or batch. Custom models need explanation metadata and parameters at upload or deployment; AutoML tabular configures itself |
| Has production data drifted from training? | [Model Monitoring](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/model-monitoring/monitor-explainable-ai): aggregate skew and drift, not one decision |
| Which dataset and pipeline built this model? | [ML Metadata](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/ml-metadata/introduction) lineage |
| Who called the endpoint, and with what input? | [Audit logs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/audit-logging) record `predict` calls (Data Access logs are off by default); [request-response logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/online-prediction-logging) stores payloads |

Vertex Explainable AI is **deprecated**: no new features since March 16, 2026, APIs end March 16, 2027, and Google points to open-source SHAP and LIME ([deprecations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/deprecations)). Keep the requirement, not the product.

## AI Hypercomputer and accelerators

[AI Hypercomputer](https://cloud.google.com/ai-hypercomputer/docs/overview) is an integrated supercomputing system for AI and ML, not a single SKU. It has three layers:

1. **Performance-optimized infrastructure:** NVIDIA GPUs and Google Cloud TPUs, plus networking and storage tuned for AI.
2. **Open software:** PyTorch, JAX and TensorFlow, orchestrated with GKE, Slurm through Cluster Director, or Cluster Toolkit blueprints.
3. **Flexible consumption:** Flex-start VMs, Spot VMs, reservations, and Dynamic Workload Scheduler for atomic provisioning of interconnected node blocks.

The aim is goodput: the share of time spent making ML progress.

### TPU versus GPU versus CPU

The [Cloud TPU overview](https://cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/intro-to-tpu) frames the choice. TPUs are Google-designed ASICs with on-chip high-bandwidth memory that group into **slices**, using the XLA compiler. They excel for matrix-heavy models, training that runs for weeks or months, large models with large batches, and ranking or recommendation workloads. GPUs fit models with custom PyTorch or JAX operations that must run on the CPU, and TensorFlow operations unavailable on TPU. CPUs suit prototyping, simple models, and I/O-bound workloads.

### Consumption options for scarce accelerators

The [consumption models](https://cloud.google.com/ai-hypercomputer/docs/consumption-models) trade price, duration and capacity assurance:

| Option | Duration | Assurance and price | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-demand | Any | Lowest assurance, standard price | Inference, prototyping |
| Spot VMs | Reclaimable at any time | Best effort; up to 91% off | Fault-tolerant batch and checkpointed training |
| Flex-start | Up to 7 days | Provisioned when available; up to 53% off on select series | Fine-tuning, small pre-training, HPC simulation |
| Future reservation, calendar mode | Up to 90 days | Very high; exclusive access | Time-boxed distributed training or large-scale inference |
| Future reservation, capacity blocks | Long-running | Highest; commitment of one year or longer for discounts | Foundation model pre-training |

GPU reservations can carry sharing policies so Agent Platform training and prediction jobs consume them ([reservations overview](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/reservations-overview)). Remember the Compute Engine rule: a commitment gives a discount, not guaranteed capacity.

## Model Garden and choosing a model

[Model Garden](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/start/explore-models) is the hub to discover, test and deploy models. It groups **first-party** models (the Gemini family plus specialized models such as Veo and Lyria), **open models** (for example Llama, Mistral and DeepSeek variants), **partner models** (including Anthropic's Claude) and task-specific models. Deployment is either **managed access** through Model-as-a-Service or direct API calls with minimal infrastructure, or **self-deployment** of open models to your own endpoints on GPUs or TPUs, with a Private Service Connect interface keeping traffic private. Each model has its own licence terms (see [using Model Garden models](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-garden/use-models)). Choose managed access for no infrastructure; self-deploy for a specific open model, isolation or tuned serving.

## Prebuilt AI APIs

When the task is a standard perception, language or extraction problem, call a managed API instead of training anything:

| API | What it does |
|---|---|
| [Cloud Vision API](https://cloud.google.com/vision/docs/features-list) | Label detection, OCR, document text detection for dense text and handwriting, object localization with bounding boxes, face, landmark and logo detection, SafeSearch |
| [Natural Language API](https://cloud.google.com/natural-language/docs/basics) | Sentiment, entity and entity-sentiment analysis, syntax, content classification into predefined categories, text moderation; input is text or a Cloud Storage URI |
| [Speech-to-Text](https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests) | Synchronous recognition for audio of 1 minute or less, asynchronous for up to 480 minutes, streaming for live audio |
| [Document AI](https://cloud.google.com/document-ai/docs/overview) | Processors that digitize (OCR), extract (Form Parser, pretrained invoice and tax-form processors, custom extractors) and classify documents |

Prebuilt APIs need no cluster or GPU provisioning. Document AI creates **processor** instances per project, each with a prediction endpoint.

**[Gemini Cloud Assist](https://cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/cloud-assist/overview)** is an AI collaborator for operating Google Cloud (infrastructure code, diagnosing issues, cost analysis), not a model-serving or training product.

## Generating versus editing images

Decide by input. Text in, new image out is **generation**. An existing image plus an instruction in, changed image out (color variants, a new background, added text) is **editing**; Cymbal's base-image variations are editing. Current Gemini image models do both, including [multi-turn editing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/multimodal/gemini-edit-images) from an image plus a text prompt. Imagen generation endpoints were [deprecated](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/release-notes) in March 2026 with a June 30, 2026 migration deadline to Gemini image models, so Imagen material is dated. The **Vision API analyzes** images and cannot create or edit them; **AutoML classifiers** assign labels, not pixels.

## Choosing between APIs, AutoML, Gemini, and custom training

Google's [training-method guidance](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/start/training-methods) and its [AI/ML decision tree](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/pick-your-aiml-path-google-cloud) share one rule of thumb: use pretrained models whenever they fit, because building and maintaining a high-quality model takes effort and expertise. Escalate only when the fit fails.

| Approach | Fits when | Costs you |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-trained API (Vision, Natural Language, Speech-to-Text) | A generic task, no training data | Nothing to train; fixed categories |
| AutoML | The API lacks your labels, the team has limited ML experience, or you want a quick baseline on image or tabular data | A labeled dataset; you must target one of its predefined objectives |
| Gemini | Generative, summarization, extraction or multimodal reasoning from a prompt | Prompt design; grounding or tuning if needed |
| Custom training | You need control of architecture, framework or exported assets, or mixed inputs such as images plus tabular metadata | ML expertise and code, plus compute |

With Gemini, **start with prompting**, add RAG or grounding when answers must cite sources or use fresh or private data, and use supervised fine-tuning for a well-defined task such as classification or structured output, with input-output example pairs ([guidance](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/to-tune-or-not-to-tune-a-guide-to-leveraging-your-data-with-llms)). If structured data already sits in BigQuery and your users know SQL, BigQuery ML trains in place. Example: scoring review sentiment needs the Natural Language API, transcribing calls Speech-to-Text, classifying your own defect categories AutoML image classification, and a model combining photos with sensor metadata custom training.

## Search, agents and Gemini Enterprise

The platform's [agent components](https://cloud.google.com/agent-builder/overview) are the Agent Development Kit (code-first), Agent Studio (low-code), Agent Garden (templates), Agent Runtime (managed deployment), RAG Engine and Vector Search. Three buy-versus-build rungs:

- **[Agent Search](https://cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/introduction)** (formerly Vertex AI Search and Generative AI App Builder; API `discoveryengine.googleapis.com`) is managed search and recommendations over websites, structured and unstructured data stores, with grounded answers, embedded through a search widget or the API. Choose it for enterprise search or Q&A with no retrieval pipeline to run; build with RAG Engine or Vector Search only when you need control of chunking and ranking.
- **[Gemini Enterprise](https://cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/overview)** is the employee-facing product: permissions-aware search across connected sources (Confluence, Jira, SharePoint, ServiceNow), an assistant, and [agents](https://cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/agents-overview).
- **[Gemini Notebook Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)** (formerly NotebookLM Enterprise) grounds answers in documents a team uploads (300 sources per notebook), with data staying in your project (VPC-SC, CMEK) and a console-configured URL.

Rule: cited answers over a team's uploads, no build: Gemini Notebook Enterprise; end-user knowledge work with permissions-aware search across connected company sources: Gemini Enterprise; embedding search or agents inside your own application: Agent Search and the Agent Platform.

### Retail product discovery: AI Commerce Search

[AI Commerce Search](https://cloud.google.com/retail/docs/overview) in Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience is the managed service for ecommerce **search, browse and recommendations**. It was rebranded in June 2026 from **Vertex AI Search for commerce**, itself renamed in January 2025 from Vertex AI Search for retail and earlier Retail Search ([release notes](https://cloud.google.com/retail/docs/release-notes)). Older material may say Retail API or Discovery AI; the API is still `retail.googleapis.com`.

You do not train anything. You ingest a **product catalog** (one `default_catalog` per project; each product needs `id`, `title` and at least one category; upload is free, ideally daily for fast-changing catalogs) and **user events** ([events guide](https://cloud.google.com/retail/docs/user-events)): home-page-view, search, category-page-view, detail-page-view, add-to-cart, shopping-cart-page-view and purchase-complete, sent by JavaScript pixel, Google Tag Manager, the real-time write API, or bulk import from BigQuery or Cloud Storage. Google trains the [recommendation models](https://cloud.google.com/retail/docs/models) on that data: Recommended for You (homepage), Others You May Like, Frequently Bought Together (cart and detail pages), Buy It Again, On-Sale, Similar Items (catalog only, no events) and Page-Level Optimization. Objectives are click-through rate (default), conversion rate or revenue per session. Initial training takes 2 to 5 days, and each model has event thresholds; Frequently Bought Together needs at least 1,000 purchase-complete events in the last year.

Choose it over Agent Search when the data is a **retail catalog** with shopper behavior, and over a custom recommender because merchandising controls come built in and rollout includes A/B experiments. Anti-patterns: launching with sparse events, caching personalized results or returning them to another user, or switching catalog branches when using recommendations.

## Agent or deterministic workflow?

Google's [design-pattern guidance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/choose-design-pattern-agentic-ai-system) splits on whether the path is known. **Deterministic** tasks are predictable and sequential; if a workload is highly structured, or fits one model call, non-agentic solutions are more cost effective. **Dynamic orchestration** is for problems where agents decide how to proceed without a script. Rule: fully specified steps and API calls go to an orchestrator (Workflows, Cloud Run, Cloud Composer); use an agent only for interpreting unstructured input or judgment across tools. Hybrids are normal: a fixed flow with one model call to read free text.

**Human approval.** Workflows [callbacks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/workflows/docs/creating-callback-endpoints) pause an execution: `events.create_callback_endpoint` returns a URL and `events.await_callback` waits for a request to it. The default timeout is 12 hours, then `TimeoutError`: set a timeout covering the approval window and catch it to escalate. Callers need `workflows.callbacks.send`; only the creating execution can wait.

## Conversational Agents (Dialogflow CX) versus Dialogflow ES versus custom

The [Conversational Agents console](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/console-conversational-agents) is the current interface for Dialogflow CX; it replaces the deprecated Dialogflow CX and Vertex AI Agent Builder consoles and builds agents from generative playbooks, deterministic flows and data stores. The [editions page](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/docs/editions) positions **Dialogflow ES** as the standard type for small to medium applications (flat intents) and **CX** as the advanced type for large or complex ones (flows and pages as a state machine, built-in test cases, DTMF, redaction).

| Option | Pick it when | You carry |
|---|---|---|
| Dialogflow ES | A small, simple intent bot | Limits as dialogs branch and grow |
| Conversational Agents (CX) | Multi-turn branching, voice and chat channels, human handoff, environments | Flow design and webhook code |
| Custom (Cloud Run plus Gemini) | A single generative feature inside your own product | Session state, channels, telephony, handoff and testing, all yours |

- **Channels.** CX has built-in [integrations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/integration) (Phone Gateway, Messenger, Slack, Google Chat) and partner telephony (AudioCodes, Avaya, Twilio, Voximplant).
- **Environments.** [Versions deploy to custom environments](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/version) such as testing and production, which integrations or API callers can name. [Webhook URL and authentication can be set per environment](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/webhook), so one agent can send a channel to its own isolated webhook backend.
- **Human handoff.** The [handoff documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-cx/agent-assist/handoff-cx) describes transferring a conversation from a CX agent to a human agent, so escalation is a platform feature, not something to build.
- **Grounding.** [Data store tools](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/data-store/handler) answer from public web, unstructured or structured (FAQ) data. [Hybrid agents](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/data-store/hybrid) suit questions answerable from your documents, not database lookups or deterministic responses.
- **Agent Assist is for humans.** It gives [real-time suggestions to human agents](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/docs) during live conversations. It does not answer callers, so it cannot deflect calls; a virtual agent does.

## Scenario walkthroughs

**Claims-processing startup, no ML team.** Scanned claim forms must become structured records, and damage photos must be labeled. Answer: Document AI processors for the forms and the Vision API for labels; if generic labels prove too coarse, AutoML Vision Object Detection.

**Pre-training a large model with a fixed launch date.** Thousands of interconnected accelerators for weeks, no tolerance for capacity surprises. Answer: AI Hypercomputer with a future reservation (capacity blocks for the longest runs, calendar mode up to 90 days) and checkpointing. Spot is wrong for the critical path; Flex-start caps at seven days.

## Anti-patterns and common mistakes

- **Training a custom model for a solved problem, or jumping to fine-tuning first.** OCR, sentiment, transcription and invoices have prebuilt APIs; try prompting, then grounding, then tuning; try the API before AutoML.
- **Orchestrating ML with cron, VMs or chained functions.** Use Pipelines.
- **Buying a long commitment to secure accelerators, or Spot for unrecoverable long training.** A CUD is a discount, not capacity; Spot is fine with checkpointing, otherwise a reclaim loses days of work.
- **Buying Agent Assist to deflect calls.** It coaches human agents; deflection needs a virtual agent such as CX.
- **Building a multi-channel, handoff-capable support bot from scratch on Cloud Run and Gemini.** You would rebuild state, channels, handoff and testing that CX provides; conversely, CX is overkill for one generative feature in your own app.
- **Copying BigQuery data to CSV in a bucket for every training run,** or **adding Model Monitoring and expecting it to prevent skew.** Read BigQuery directly; share feature definitions to prevent skew and monitor to detect it.
- **Hand-building RAG for plain document search.** Agent Search is managed grounding and ranking.
- **Hand-building a retail recommender, or using general Agent Search for a product catalog.** AI Commerce Search is built for catalogs and shopper events.
- **Wrapping a fixed API sequence in an agent.** It adds cost and variance; keep a workflow.
- **Asking Vision to edit, AutoML to generate, or Model Monitoring to explain one decision.**

## Exam tips

- **Repeatable preprocess-train-evaluate-deploy DAG:** Agent Platform Pipelines (KFP or TFX), not VMs, Cloud Functions chains or scheduled queries.
- **Large-scale training and serving fabric:** AI Hypercomputer, built on TPUs and GPUs with high-bandwidth networking. **Catalog to discover, test, tune and deploy Gemini, open and partner models:** Model Garden.
- **Prebuilt first:** Vision for labels and OCR, Natural Language for sentiment and entities, Speech-to-Text for transcription, Document AI for structured extraction. AutoML when the API lacks your labels or the team lacks ML skills; Gemini with prompting first, then grounding, then tuning; custom training for architecture control or mixed inputs.
- **Secure scarce accelerators with reservations or Flex-start.** Calendar mode reaches up to 90 days; Flex-start up to 7 days; capacity blocks for long pre-training.
- **Vertex AI and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform are the same product.** Expect either name.
- **Same features for training and serving, sourced from BigQuery:** Feature Store prevents the divergence; Model Monitoring only detects skew and drift. Training reads BigQuery directly. Cloud Run functions are event glue, not orchestration.
- **Multi-turn virtual agent with voice and chat channels and human handoff:** Conversational Agents (Dialogflow CX), with environments and per-environment webhooks to isolate stages or channels. ES suits small simple bots; custom Cloud Run plus Gemini means you build state and handoff; Agent Assist does not deflect calls.
- **Retail site search, browse and recommendations from catalog plus user events:** AI Commerce Search (formerly Vertex AI Search for commerce). Generic document search: Agent Search.
- **Employee assistant over company data:** Gemini Enterprise. Cited answers from a team's uploads: Gemini Notebook Enterprise. Search inside your own app: Agent Search.
- **Why did this input get this score?** Per-prediction feature attributions (Explainable AI, sunset March 2027). Aggregate drift: Model Monitoring. Model-to-data trace: ML Metadata lineage. Who called: audit logs.
- **Variants of a supplied image:** editing with a Gemini image model; text only: generation. Vision analyzes only.
- **Known steps and API calls:** a workflow, not an agent. **Human approval:** Workflows callback with an explicit timeout.
- **Model Registry, Feature Store, Experiments and Model Monitoring** are the lifecycle components around Pipelines; match each to its single job.
